Let \(\chi\) be the quadratic character of \(\mathbb F_p\), with \(\chi(0)=0\). A unit of \(\mathbb Z/p^\alpha\mathbb Z\) is a square iff its reduction mod \(p\) is a nonzero square, so adjacency in \(G_{p,\alpha}\) depends only on residues mod \(p\).

Thus \(G_{p,\alpha}\) is obtained from the Paley graph \(P_p\) on \(\mathbb F_p\) by replacing each vertex by an independent fibre of size \(p^{\alpha-1}\). A \(4\)-clique in \(G_{p,\alpha}\) therefore projects to a \(4\)-clique in \(P_p\), with \(p^{4(\alpha-1)}\) lifts.

It remains to count \(4\)-cliques in \(P_p\). For the Paley graph, the number of unordered \(4\)-cliques is

\[
K_4(P_p)=\frac{p(p-1)}{1536}\Bigl((p-9)^2-16v^2\Bigr).
\]

Here is the relevant character-count in brief. Fix an edge \(\{0,1\}\). Its common-neighbour set is

\[
N=\{x\in\mathbb F_p:\chi(x)=\chi(x-1)=1\}.
\]

Let \(e\) be the number of edges inside \(N\). Expanding the indicator

\[
\frac{1+\chi(x)}2\frac{1+\chi(x-1)}2
\]

and evaluating the resulting quartic Jacobi sums gives

\[
e=\frac{(p-9)^2-16v^2}{64}.
\]

Since \(P_p\) has \(p(p-1)/4\) edges and each \(4\)-clique contains \(6\) edges,

\[
K_4(P_p)=\frac{1}{6}\cdot \frac{p(p-1)}4\cdot e
=\frac{p(p-1)}{1536}\Delta_p.
\]

Therefore

\[
C_{p,\alpha}
=
p^{4(\alpha-1)}K_4(P_p)
=
\frac{p^{4\alpha-3}(p-1)\Delta_p}{1536}.
\]

Now impose the zero-sum condition. Translation acts freely on the set of \(4\)-cliques in \(P_p\), and every translation orbit contains exactly one clique with sum \(0\), because for a clique \(S\),

\[
\sum_{x\in(S+t)}x=\sum_{x\in S}x+4t,
\]

and \(4\) is invertible mod \(p\). Hence the number of zero-sum \(4\)-cliques in \(P_p\) is \(K_4(P_p)/p\).

For each zero-sum residue clique, the lifts satisfy one linear congruence over \(p^{\alpha-1}\), so there are \(p^{3(\alpha-1)}\) zero-sum lifts. Thus

\[
Z_{p,\alpha}
=
p^{3(\alpha-1)}\frac{K_4(P_p)}p
=
\frac{p^{3\alpha-3}(p-1)\Delta_p}{1536}.
\]

\[
\boxed{
(C_{p,\alpha},Z_{p,\alpha})
=
\left(
\frac{p^{4\alpha-3}(p-1)\Delta_p}{1536},
\frac{p^{3\alpha-3}(p-1)\Delta_p}{1536}
\right)
}
\]
